summary: Lowndes County lookout that served Kinderlou Forest from 1939 to 1993; its tower now stands at Grand Bay WMA, where a DNR notice dated 10/8/26 closes the boardwalk.

facts.status_note: The 54-foot tower served Kinderlou Forest from 1939 to 1993; the sources suggest it now stands at the end of the Grand Bay boardwalk. No source describes the Kinderlou Forest site today.

access.note: Applies to the tower at Grand Bay. The DNR notice posted 10/8/26 says the boardwalk is closed until further notice. The Kinderlou Forest site's access is not described.

visit.trail_note: Reached by a half-mile boardwalk from the Grand Bay Wetland Education Center. The boardwalk is closed until further notice per the DNR notice posted 10/8/26.

events.note: Start of fire-lookout service in Kinderlou Forest, per the 2012 photo essay. Construction date not given.
End of fire-lookout service in Kinderlou Forest, per the 2012 photo essay.
DNR notice posted 10/8/26: the Grand Bay boardwalk, which ends at the tower, is closed until further notice.

notes_for_editor: Identity and move: the list's grand bay entry (GA425) carries the note Ron GA097-relocated, and GA097 is kinderlou. The 2012 essay says the 54-foot Kinderlou Tower served in Kinderlou Forest from 1939 to 1993, and the Encyclopedia and essay tie the same tower to the Grand Bay boardwalk. The move is inferred from those links; no source dates it or describes it, so no relocation event is recorded. Height is the essay's 54 ft converted to metres. Construction date, builder and design are not in any source read. The list's kinderlou coordinates are its own; the list's grand bay point is roughly 21 km northeast of them by our calculation, so the two list points do not coincide. The old kinderlou entry (GA232) is about 1.6 km away by our calculation; no source explains it, and it may or may not be the earlier site. Access: the DNR notice dated 10/8/26 closes the boardwalk; an undated gate alert on the same page gives hours. The story follows the dated notice; recheck with DNR before giving visit advice. Elevation 213 in the list is unitless and is not used in the story. Not used: the 2012 essay's climbing, wasp and GORP remarks, which are dated. Searches: two web searches; the Forest Fire Lookout Association Georgia index had no kinderlou line in the crawl. The Kinderlou Forest neighbourhood site home page was read but has no tower content; its history article was not read. Page reads ran over the six-read budget (about eight distinct pages, several cached and re-grepped), because the Grand Bay sources were needed to confirm the move. Sources shared with us-ga-grand-bay; the quotes are from the same cached pages.
